newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban take strategic Salang Pass.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban take strategic Salang Pass.

text.p: The Taleban Islamic militia captured the strategic Salang Pass in northern Afghanistan on Sunday, witnesses said.
They said the pass fell at 5.30 p.m.(1300 gmt) when a commander of forces defending it struck a deal with the Taleban, which now controls over two thirds of the country.
A Reuter correspondent at Salang said the opposition commander, Basir Salangi, radioed to his men not to shoot at the Taleban moving up the road.
Hundreds of Taleban troops, in a jubilant mood, waited in trucks, cars and tanks to move across the front line.
The Salang Pass, built by the former Soviet Union, lies on the main highway leading from Kabul to Central Asia.
